final_message:
I fixed `int_to_roman` in `src/roman.py`, but I couldn't run it to confirm.

The function only had the seven basic symbols, so it could never produce subtractive forms. I added the six missing pairs (`CM`, `CD`, `XC`, `XL`, `IX`, `IV`) to the lookup table. Tracing the table by hand, `int_to_roman(4)` now returns `'IV'`, and 1994 gives `'MCMXCIV'`. The loop logic is unchanged.

My first check failed because I ran Python with `-I`, which dropped the current directory from the import path. When I retried with `PYTHONPATH`, Bash was denied in this session. I haven't run any check on the fix.

The check I wanted compares `int_to_roman(4)` and `int_to_roman(1994)` with their expected values. It also confirms `roman_to_int(int_to_roman(i)) == i` for every `i` from 1 to 3999. If you'd like me to run it, allow Bash and I'll do that.
